functions.name: hash32
functions.signature: u32 hash32(u8 *key, u32 len, u32 seed);
functions.description: Computes a 32-bit hash of the provided byte buffer. Intended for fast, non-cryptographic hashing in AFL++ utilities. Exact algorithm and properties are not documented in this header; typical usage is hashing len bytes starting at key with a 32-bit seed to influence the result.
requirements: key must point to at least len bytes of readable memory.
len is the number of bytes to hash.
seed is an arbitrary 32-bit value that perturbs the result.
Behavior for key == NULL when len == 0 is unknown (not documented).

functions.name: hash64
functions.signature: u64 hash64(u8 *key, u32 len, u64 seed);
functions.description: Computes a 64-bit hash of the provided byte buffer. Intended for fast, non-cryptographic hashing in AFL++ utilities. Exact algorithm and properties are not documented in this header; typical usage is hashing len bytes starting at key with a 64-bit seed to influence the result.
requirements: key must point to at least len bytes of readable memory.
len is the number of bytes to hash.
seed is an arbitrary 64-bit value that perturbs the result.
Behavior for key == NULL when len == 0 is unknown (not documented).

functions.name: XXH_versionNumber
functions.description: Returns the xxHash library version number encoded as (MAJOR*100*100 + MINOR*100 + RELEASE). Useful when xxHash is built as a shared library to query the runtime version.
requirements: No arguments; callable at any time.

functions.name: XXH32
functions.signature: XXH32_hash_t XXH32(const void *input, size_t length, XXH32_hash_t seed);
functions.description: Computes a 32-bit xxHash (XXH32) of a contiguous memory block in a single call. This is the fastest and simplest way to hash small or medium inputs.
requirements: If length == 0, input may be NULL; otherwise input must point to at least length readable bytes.
For C++, the input object range must be TriviallyCopyable (bytes accessed as unsigned char).

functions.name: XXH32_createState
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new XXH32 streaming state object used for incremental hashing.
requirements: Returns NULL on allocation failure.
The returned state must be freed with XXH32_freeState().
Do not free with free(); use the provided API.

functions.name: XXH32_freeState
functions.description: Frees a state previously allocated by XXH32_createState().
requirements: statePtr must have been allocated by XXH32_createState().
Safe to pass a statePtr previously returned by XXH32_createState(); returns XXH_OK.

functions.name: XXH32_copyState
functions.description: Copies the complete XXH32 streaming state from src_state to dst_state.
requirements: dst_state must not be NULL.
src_state must not be NULL.
dst_state and src_state must not overlap.

functions.name: XXH32_reset
functions.description: Initializes or re-initializes an XXH32 streaming state to start a new hashing session with the provided 32-bit seed.
requirements: statePtr must not be NULL.
Call before XXH32_update() for a new session.

functions.name: XXH32_update
functions.signature: XXH_errorcode XXH32_update(XXH32_state_t *statePtr, const void *input, size_t length);
functions.description: Ingests a block of data into an XXH32 streaming state. Can be called repeatedly to hash data incrementally.
requirements: statePtr must not be NULL.
If length == 0, input may be NULL; otherwise input must point to at least length readable bytes.
For C++, the input range must be TriviallyCopyable.
Returns XXH_OK on success, XXH_ERROR on failure.

functions.name: XXH32_digest
functions.description: Finalizes and returns the current 32-bit hash value from an XXH32 streaming state without modifying the state, allowing further updates and digests.
requirements: statePtr must not be NULL.

functions.name: XXH32_canonicalFromHash
functions.description: Converts a native-endian XXH32 hash value to its canonical big-endian byte representation for portable storage or transmission.
requirements: dst must not be NULL.

functions.name: XXH32_hashFromCanonical
functions.description: Converts a canonical big-endian XXH32 byte representation back to a native-endian XXH32 hash value.
requirements: src must not be NULL.

functions.name: XXH64
functions.signature: XXH64_hash_t XXH64(const void *input, size_t length, XXH64_hash_t seed);
functions.description: Computes a 64-bit xxHash (XXH64) of a contiguous memory block in a single call. Prefer for 64-bit targets or when a 64-bit output is desired.
requirements: If length == 0, input may be NULL; otherwise input must point to at least length readable bytes.
For C++, the input object range must be TriviallyCopyable (bytes accessed as unsigned char).

functions.name: XXH64_createState

requirements: statePtr must have been allocated by XXH64_createState().
Returns XXH_OK.

functions.name: XXH64_copyState
functions.description: Copies the complete XXH64 streaming state from src_state to dst_state.
requirements: dst_state must not be NULL.
src_state must not be NULL.
dst_state and src_state must not overlap.

functions.description: Initializes or re-initializes an XXH64 streaming state to start a new hashing session with the provided 64-bit seed.
requirements: statePtr must not be NULL.

functions.name: XXH64_update
functions.signature: XXH_errorcode XXH64_update(XXH64_state_t *statePtr, const void *input, size_t length);
functions.description: Ingests a block of data into an XXH64 streaming state. Can be called repeatedly to hash data incrementally.
requirements: statePtr must not be NULL.
If length == 0, input may be NULL; otherwise input must point to at least length readable bytes.
For C++, the input range must be TriviallyCopyable.
Returns XXH_OK on success, XXH_ERROR on failure.

functions.name: XXH64_digest
functions.description: Finalizes and returns the current 64-bit hash value from an XXH64 streaming state without modifying the state, allowing further updates and digests.
requirements: statePtr must not be NULL.

functions.name: XXH64_canonicalFromHash
functions.description: Converts a native-endian XXH64 hash value to its canonical big-endian byte representation for portable storage or transmission.
requirements: dst must not be NULL.

functions.name: XXH64_hashFromCanonical
functions.description: Converts a canonical big-endian XXH64 byte representation back to a native-endian XXH64 hash value.
requirements: src must not be NULL.

functions.name: XXH3_64bits
functions.description: Computes the unseeded 64-bit XXH3 hash of a contiguous memory block. Optimized for both small and large inputs; benefits from SIMD when available.
requirements: If length == 0, input may be NULL; otherwise input must point to at least length readable bytes.
For C++, the input range must be TriviallyCopyable.

functions.name: XXH3_64bits_withSecret
functions.signature: XXH64_hash_t XXH3_64bits_withSecret(const void *input, size_t length, const void *secret, size_t secretSize);
functions.description: Computes the 64-bit XXH3 hash using a caller-provided secret blob to increase dispersion and collision resistance for adversarial inputs.
requirements: input must reference at least length readable bytes; may be NULL if length == 0.
secret must not be NULL.
secretSize must be >= XXH3_SECRET_SIZE_MIN (136).
The secret should be high-entropy random-looking bytes; low-entropy secrets degrade distribution.

functions.name: XXH3_64bits_withSeed
functions.signature: XXH64_hash_t XXH3_64bits_withSeed(const void *input, size_t length, XXH64_hash_t seed);
functions.description: Computes the 64-bit XXH3 hash with a 64-bit seed. Internally derives a secret from the seed; seed == 0 is equivalent to XXH3_64bits().
requirements: If length == 0, input may be NULL; otherwise input must point to at least length readable bytes.
For C++, the input range must be TriviallyCopyable.

functions.name: XXH3_64bits_withSecretandSeed
functions.signature: XXH64_hash_t XXH3_64bits_withSecretandSeed(const void *input, size_t length, const void *secret, size_t secretSize, XXH64_hash_t seed);
functions.description: Computes the 64-bit XXH3 hash using both a secret and a seed. Uses the seed for short inputs and the secret for large inputs to combine performance and strength.
requirements: If length == 0, input may be NULL; otherwise input must point to at least length readable bytes.
secret must not be NULL for large inputs; secretSize must be >= XXH3_SECRET_SIZE_MIN (136).
When the secret was generated via XXH3_generateSecret_fromSeed(), this produces identical results to the _withSeed variant for small inputs while avoiding regenerating the secret for large inputs.

functions.name: XXH3_createState
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new XXH3 streaming state object used for incremental hashing for both 64-bit and 128-bit XXH3 variants. The state is sufficiently aligned for SIMD implementations.
requirements: Returns NULL on allocation failure.
The returned state must be freed with XXH3_freeState().
Do not free with free(); use the provided API.

functions.name: XXH3_freeState
functions.description: Frees an XXH3 state previously allocated by XXH3_createState().
requirements: statePtr must have been allocated by XXH3_createState().
Returns XXH_OK.

functions.name: XXH3_copyState
functions.description: Copies one XXH3 streaming state to another. Works for both 64-bit and 128-bit XXH3 modes since they share the same state type.
requirements: dst_state must not be NULL.
src_state must not be NULL.
dst_state and src_state must not overlap.

functions.name: XXH3_64bits_reset
functions.description: Resets an XXH3 state for a new 64-bit unseeded hashing session. Generates a default internal secret.
requirements: statePtr must not be NULL.
Call before XXH3_64bits_update().
Digest result will be equivalent to XXH3_64bits().

functions.name: XXH3_64bits_reset_withSeed
functions.description: Resets an XXH3 state for a new 64-bit hashing session using the provided 64-bit seed (derives an internal secret from the seed).
requirements: statePtr must not be NULL.
Call before XXH3_64bits_update().
Digest result will be equivalent to XXH3_64bits_withSeed().

functions.description: Resets an XXH3 state for a new 64-bit hashing session using an external secret. The secret is referenced and must remain valid for the duration of the session.
requirements: statePtr must not be NULL.
secret must not be NULL and must outlive the streaming session.
secretSize must be >= XXH3_SECRET_SIZE_MIN (136).

functions.name: XXH3_128bits

requirements: If len == 0, input may be NULL; otherwise input must point to at least len readable bytes.

data_types.description: A raw byte buffer with no required encoding or structure. Any sequence of bytes of length N>=0. Used directly as input to hashing functions; may be empty (length 0) or up to the provided cap.

A byte buffer intended to serve as a secret for XXH3 *_withSecret* APIs. Must be at least 136 bytes long and should contain random-looking, high-entropy data. No specific format beyond size and randomness; used verbatim as the secret blob.

generators.generator:
import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid arbitrary binary data buffers suitable for xxHash APIs.
# Goals:
# - Cover empty, small, medium, and near-cap inputs (up to 2048 used by stubs; keep <=4096 here).
# - Mix content types: zeroes, 0xFF, ascending/descending sequences, repeating patterns, UTF-8-ish text,
#   random bytes, structured numeric patterns, and aligned lengths common to hash block sizes (e.g., 16/32/64).
# - Occasionally embed a plausible xxHash secret region (>=136 bytes) so that if FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME or STR is
#   reused for secret source in the stub, it already satisfies the minimum size without padding.
# - Deterministic per-seed but varied across calls.

MAX_OUT = 4096

def _choose_lengths(rng: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    # Bias towards interesting boundaries used by xxHash (0, 1..16, 32, 64, 128, 136, 192, 255, 256, 512, 1024, 1536, 2048)
    candidates = [
        0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 17,
        31, 32, 33, 63, 64, 65,
        95, 96, 127, 128, 129,
        135, 136, 137, 191, 192, 193,
        255, 256, 257, 511, 512, 513,
        1023, 1024, 1500, 1536, 1700, 1792,
        2000, 2048, 3072
    ]
    # Add a few random sizes up to 3000 to diversify
    for _ in range(5):
        candidates.append(rng.randint(0, 3000))
    # Ensure sizes do not exceed MAX_OUT
    sizes = [s for s in candidates if s <= MAX_OUT]
    # Pick one weighted: prefer small/medium with some chance of large
    weights = []
    for s in sizes:
        if s == 0:
            w = 3
        elif s <= 64:
            w = 5
        elif s <= 256:
            w = 4
        elif s <= 1024:
            w = 3
        elif s <= 2048:
            w = 2
        else:
            w = 1
        weights.append(w)
    return [rng.choices(sizes, weights=weights, k=1)[0]][:1]


def _pattern_zero(n: int) -> bytes:
    return b"\x00" * n


def _pattern_ff(n: int) -> bytes:
    return b"\xff" * n


def _pattern_ascending(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((i % 256 for i in range(n)))


def _pattern_descending(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(((255 - (i % 256)) for i in range(n)))


def _pattern_repeat(chunk: bytes, n: int) -> bytes:
    if not chunk:
        return b""
    reps, rem = divmod(n, len(chunk))
    return chunk * reps + chunk[:rem]


def _pattern_utf8ish(n: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Mix ASCII text with some multibyte UTF-8 sequences
    words = [
        b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.",
        b"xxHash", b"XXH32", b"XXH64", b"XXH3", b"128bits", b"seed", b"secret",
        b"AFL++", b"fuzz", b"hash", b"stream", b"update", b"digest",
    ]
    multibyte = [
        b"\xC2\xA9",  # ©
        b"\xE2\x9C\x93",  # ✓
        b"\xE2\x98\x83",  # ☃
        b"\xF0\x9F\x92\xA9",  # 💩
    ]
    buf = bytearray()
    while len(buf) < n:
        if rng.random() < 0.8:
            w = rng.choice(words)
        else:
            w = rng.choice(multibyte)
        buf.extend(w)
        buf.append(0x0A)
    return bytes(buf[:n])


def _pattern_numeric_series(n: int) -> bytes:
    # Fill with alternating little/big endian 32-bit integers and a 64-bit counter
    out = bytearray()
    val32 = 0x9E3779B1
    val64 = 0x0123456789ABCDEF
    toggle = False
    while len(out) + 8 <= n:
        if toggle:
            out += struct.pack(">I", val32 & 0xFFFFFFFF)
        else:
            out += struct.pack("<I", val32 & 0xFFFFFFFF)
        out += struct.pack("<Q", val64 & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)
        val32 = (val32 * 2654435761 + 1013904223) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        val64 = (val64 * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 + 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
        toggle = not toggle
    # Tail with ascending
    rem = n - len(out)
    if rem > 0:
        out += _pattern_ascending(rem)
    return bytes(out)


def _maybe_embed_secret(buf: bytearray, rng: random.Random) -> None:
    # With some probability, append a >=136-byte region that resembles a secret
    if len(buf) >= 3000:
        return
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        secret_len = rng.choice([136, 160, 192, 224, 256, 320, 384, 512])
        secret_len = min(secret_len, MAX_OUT - len(buf))
        if secret_len <= 0:
            return
        # Create high-entropy-like secret: mix random, counter, and constants
        sec = bytearray(os.urandom(secret_len))
        for i in range(0, secret_len, 16):
            # XOR in a structured lane to avoid being purely random
            lane = struct.pack("<QQ", i, (i * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)
            for j in range(min(16, secret_len - i)):
                sec[i + j] ^= lane[j]
        buf += sec


def _build_buffer(n: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose a base pattern
    patterns = []
    patterns.append(_pattern_zero)
    patterns.append(_pattern_ff)
    patterns.append(_pattern_ascending)
    patterns.append(_pattern_descending)
    patterns.append(lambda m: _pattern_repeat(b"\x00\xFF", m))
    patterns.append(lambda m: _pattern_repeat(b"\xAA\x55", m))
    patterns.append(lambda m: _pattern_repeat(b"xxh3_secret", m))
    patterns.append(lambda m: _pattern_utf8ish(m, rng))
    patterns.append(_pattern_numeric_series)

    # Weighted choice favoring mixed and numeric patterns
    weights = [1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 4]
    base = rng.choices(patterns, weights=weights, k=1)[0]
    buf = bytearray(base(n))

    # Occasionally splice in a second segment to create heterogenous data
    if n > 32 and rng.random() < 0.6:
        cut1 = rng.randint(0, n)
        cut2 = rng.randint(cut1, n)
        seg_len = cut2 - cut1
        if seg_len > 0:
            alt = rng.choices(patterns, weights=weights, k=1)[0]
            buf[cut1:cut2] = alt(seg_len)

    # Optionally embed a plausible secret blob at the end to satisfy secret-bearing stubs
    _maybe_embed_secret(buf, rng)

    # Trim to MAX_OUT
    if len(buf) > MAX_OUT:
        del buf[MAX_OUT:]
    return bytes(buf)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Pick one interesting size
    sizes = _choose_lengths(rng)
    n = sizes[0]
    # Build buffer
    data = _build_buffer(n, rng)
    return data

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for inputs targeting XXH3_128bits_withSecret fuzzer stub.
# The stub calls FUZZ_PARAM_STR() three times potentially:
#  - First: main input bytes to hash (capped at 2048)
#  - Second: initial secret bytes
#  - Third: optional extra to reach >=136 bytes if second was too short
# Our single returned buffer must be parsable by the harness as multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
# Common AFL-style multiplexing uses simple length-prefixed chunks or delimiter-based.
# Since we don't have the exact harness, we choose a robust self-describing format:
#   [count=3 u16][chunk0_len u16][chunk0 bytes]...[chunk2_len u16][chunk2 bytes]
# This keeps chunks independent and allows arbitrary binary content.
# Each chunk is <= 4096 to satisfy total size cap; we also cap overall to 4096 bytes.
#
# Chunk semantics we generate:
#  - chunk0: input message bytes (various sizes/patterns up to 2048)
#  - chunk1: high-entropy secret (>=136 and up to 512 bytes)
#  - chunk2: extra secret tail (may be empty) — harness may append it when chunk1 < 136
# We ensure chunk1 already meets the minimum so the API sees a valid secret.
# We still populate chunk2 with additional bytes to exercise secret concatenation paths.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MIN_SECRET = 136
MAX_SECRET = 512
MAX_INPUT = 2048

# Helper: create high-entropy bytes using PRNG seeded by Python's random
# Ensures repeatability given the provided seed.
def randbytes_prng(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix different entropy sources deterministically from r
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(n // 4):
        out += struct.pack('<I', r.getrandbits(32))
    rem = n % 4
    if rem:
        val = r.getrandbits(rem * 8)
        out += val.to_bytes(rem, 'little')
    # Also inject occasional zero and 0xFF runs to vary distribution slightly
    # while keeping overall high entropy.
    if n >= 32:
        pos = r.randrange(0, max(1, n - 8))
        run = min(8, n - pos)
        fill = 0x00 if r.random() < 0.5 else 0xFF
        out[pos:pos+run] = bytes([fill]) * run
    return bytes(out[:n])

# Helper: build interesting input payloads to hash
def build_input(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    mode = r.randrange(0, 8)
    if mode == 0:
        # empty
        return b''
    elif mode == 1:
        # very small
        n = r.randrange(1, 17)
        return randbytes_prng(r, n)
    elif mode == 2:
        # medium
        n = r.randrange(17, 257)
        return randbytes_prng(r, n)
    elif mode == 3:
        # large
        n = r.randrange(257, MAX_INPUT + 1)
        return randbytes_prng(r, n)
    elif mode == 4:
        # repeated pattern
        pat_len = r.randrange(1, 33)
        pat = randbytes_prng(r, pat_len)
        reps = r.randrange(2, max(3, MAX_INPUT // max(1, pat_len)))
        data = (pat * reps)[:MAX_INPUT]
        return data
    elif mode == 5:
        # ASCII text-like with newlines and spaces
        alphabet = (b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz" \
                    b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ" \
                    b"0123456789 \t\n:_-./")
        n = r.randrange(1, MAX_INPUT + 1)
        return bytes(alphabet[r.randrange(0, len(alphabet))] for _ in range(n))
    elif mode == 6:
        # Structured-like (JSON-ish noise)
        parts = []
        count = r.randrange(1, 32)
        for i in range(count):
            key_len = r.randrange(1, 12)
            key = ''.join(chr(ord('a') + r.randrange(0, 26)) for _ in range(key_len))
            val_len = r.randrange(0, 32)
            val = randbytes_prng(r, val_len).hex()
            parts.append(f'"{key}":"{val}"')
        body = '{' + ','.join(parts) + '}'
        data = body.encode('utf-8')
        if len(data) > MAX_INPUT:
            data = data[:MAX_INPUT]
        return data
    else:
        # Mixed: prefix/suffix zeroes with random core
        core = randbytes_prng(r, r.randrange(1, MAX_INPUT + 1))
        prefix = b"\x00" * r.randrange(0, 32)
        suffix = b"\x00" * r.randrange(0, 32)
        data = (prefix + core + suffix)[:MAX_INPUT]
        return data

# Helper: build a valid secret with high entropy, >=136 and <=512
# We also prepare an extra tail chunk to test concatenation in the stub.
def build_secret_and_extra(r: random.Random) -> (bytes, bytes):
    # Choose size with bias around boundary and extremes
    choices = [MIN_SECRET, MIN_SECRET + 1, 192, 256, MAX_SECRET]
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        base_size = r.randrange(MIN_SECRET, MAX_SECRET + 1)
    else:
        base_size = choices[r.randrange(0, len(choices))]
    secret = randbytes_prng(r, base_size)

    # Ensure diversity: inject a small patterned segment occasionally
    if r.random() < 0.3 and base_size >= 64:
        start = r.randrange(0, base_size - 16)
        secret = bytearray(secret)
        secret[start:start+16] = b"ABCD" * 4
        secret = bytes(secret)

    # Extra tail optionally present
    extra_len = r.randrange(0, 65)  # up to 64 bytes
    extra = randbytes_prng(r, extra_len)
    return secret, extra

# Serialize as: [u16 count=3][u16 len0][bytes0][u16 len1][bytes1][u16 len2][bytes2]
# All lengths little-endian, each <= 4096, total bounded to 4096.
def serialize_chunks(chunks: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    header = struct.pack('<H', len(chunks))
    parts = [header]
    total = len(header) + 2 * len(chunks)  # account for length fields

    for ch in chunks:
        if len(ch) > 0xFFFF:
            ch = ch[:0xFFFF]
        parts.append(struct.pack('<H', len(ch)))
        parts.append(ch)
        total += 2 + len(ch)

    blob = b''.join(parts)
    if len(blob) > MAX_TOTAL:
        # Trim strategy: reduce chunk2, then chunk1 extra, then chunk0
        # Rebuild with trimmed sizes preserving validity
        c0, c1, c2 = chunks
        # Compute available budget
        budget = MAX_TOTAL
        out = [struct.pack('<H', 3)]
        # Reserve length fields
        budget -= 2 + 2*3
        # Assign sizes greedily under budget
        def fit(data: bytes, remaining: int) -> bytes:
            return data[:max(0, min(len(data), remaining))]
        # Allocate proportional shares but ensure minimum for secret
        # Start with c2
        remaining = budget
        c2t = fit(c2, remaining // 6 + 64)  # small share
        remaining -= len(c2t)
        # c1 (secret) must be at least MIN_SECRET
        c1max = max(MIN_SECRET, remaining - len(c0))
        c1t = c1[:min(len(c1), max(MIN_SECRET, min(c1max, MAX_SECRET)))]
        remaining -= len(c1t)
        # c0 takes the rest
        c0t = fit(c0, remaining)
        # Reassemble
        parts2 = [struct.pack('<H', 3), struct.pack('<H', len(c0t)), c0t,
                  struct.pack('<H', len(c1t)), c1t,
                  struct.pack('<H', len(c2t)), c2t]
        blob = b''.join(parts2)
        # Final safety: if still too big (edge), hard trim last chunk
        if len(blob) > MAX_TOTAL:
            over = len(blob) - MAX_TOTAL
            if len(c2t) >= over:
                c2t = c2t[:-over]
            else:
                drop = over - len(c2t)
                c2t = b''
                if len(c1t) - MIN_SECRET >= drop:
                    c1t = c1t[:-drop]
                else:
                    rem = drop - max(0, len(c1t) - MIN_SECRET)
                    c1t = c1t[:MIN_SECRET]
                    c0t = c0t[:-rem] if rem <= len(c0t) else b''
            blob = b''.join([
                struct.pack('<H', 3),
                struct.pack('<H', len(c0t)), c0t,
                struct.pack('<H', len(c1t)), c1t,
                struct.pack('<H', len(c2t)), c2t,
            ])
    return blob


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    msg = build_input(r)
    secret, extra = build_secret_and_extra(r)
    # Ensure overall cap via serializer; guarantees secret >= 136
    return serialize_chunks([msg, secret, extra])
